assembly_instructions: 1. Set the Service Module aft structural ring on the SPS thrust axis at y=1.15 m, then bolt the SPS throat, injector plate, tapered bell, exit ring, four feed lines, and paired gimbal actuators below it so the nozzle exit lip rests on y=0. 2. Add the SM mid and forward rings, four main longitudinal stringers, eight diagonal cross-braces, and narrow exterior skin staves, leaving the -X sector open as a cutaway for the SIM bay and exposed internal equipment. 3. Install the equipment shelf, avionics box, four spherical SPS propellant tanks, two cryogenic reactant tanks, two fuel-cell modules, and visible feed lines inside the open SM frame, tying each item to the mid ring or shelf. 4. Build the SIM bay in the -X sector with a floor, upper and lower side rails, mapping camera, panoramic camera, and edge radiator strip so the science-bay interruption in the SM skin is explicit. 5. Mount four RCS quad blocks at +X, -X, +Z, and -Z, then attach four individual conical thruster bells to every block. 6. Attach radiator panels and narrow skin staves between RCS stations without closing the cutaway; keep them thin enough that tanks remain visible from the ISO view. 7. Hinge the S-band high-gain antenna mast to the +X/-Z quadrant, add the yoke, square hub, four shallow dish reflectors, four dish rim rings, and four feed-support rods. 8. Stack the CM aft heat shield, lower tapered shell, mid tapered shell, and forward compartment on the SM forward ring, then add the crew hatch, umbilical fairing, docking probe, docking drogue ring, and visible cutaway rim markers. 9. Assemble the exploded CM cabin insert directly above and left of the shell: pressure-vessel ring, floor, three couches with headrests, instrument panel, forward tunnel, parachute canisters, parachute divider, and leader struts back to the CM. 10. Fasten the launch-escape tower base ring to the CM apex, install the four tower legs, joint collars, eight diagonal braces, LES solid rocket, rocket attachment ring, jettison motor, and Q-ball nose cap.

info.japanese_name: アポロ司令船・機械船 (CSM)
info.english_name: NASA Apollo Command and Service Module (CSM)
info.summary: Crewed spacecraft used on all Apollo lunar missions. A conical 3-seat Command Module rode home on the heat shield; a cylindrical Service Module carried propulsion, power, and life support.
info.description: The Apollo Command and Service Module (CSM) was the crew-carrying spacecraft of NASA's Apollo program. It consisted of two mated sections: the Command Module (CM) - a pressurized conical capsule 3.48 m tall with a 3.91 m-diameter ablative heat shield at its base, housing three astronauts and returning them to Earth; and the Service Module (SM) - a 4.52 m-long, 3.91 m-diameter cylindrical stage carrying the Service Propulsion System (SPS) main engine with a 2.50 m-diameter bell nozzle, four Reaction Control System (RCS) thruster quads at 90 degree spacing, the deployable S-band high-gain antenna with four 0.79 m dishes and a central square reflector, radiator panels, fuel cells, cryogenic propellant, and on J-missions a Scientific Instrument Module (SIM) bay recessed into one sector. A Launch Escape System tower mounted above the CM during ascent could pull the capsule clear of a failing booster; once safe staging was achieved it was jettisoned, exposing the docking probe used to mate with the Lunar Module. This scene includes an exploded CM cabin insert above the outer shell so the three couches, instrument panel, tunnel, and parachute bay can be inspected despite the opaque render.
info.contractor: North American Aviation / Rockwell (CM); North American Aviation (SM)
info.contract_date: Development contract 1961; flew Apollo 7 (Oct 1968) through Apollo-Soyuz (Jul 1975)
info.status: Retired; flown on 15 crewed Apollo/Skylab/ASTP missions

parts.name: Service Module Aft Structural Ring
parts.role: Root structural ring of the Service Module; it carries the SPS engine mount and starts the open-frame assembly.

parts.name: Service Module Mid Structural Ring
parts.role: Mid-height circular frame that ties the SM bay panels and internal equipment shelf together.

parts.name: Service Module Forward Structural Ring
parts.role: Forward SM ring that supports the Command Module heat shield and the crew umbilical fairing.

parts.name: SM +X Longitudinal Stringer
parts.role: Vertical stringer at the +X clock position; it keeps the SM cylindrical frame visible without closing the cutaway.

parts.name: SM -X Cutaway Edge Stringer
parts.role: Exposed edge stringer marking the open SIM-bay cutaway side of the SM.

parts.name: SM +Z Longitudinal Stringer
parts.role: Vertical stringer at the +Z clock position carrying one RCS quad and adjacent radiator panels.

parts.name: SM -Z Longitudinal Stringer
parts.role: Vertical stringer at the -Z clock position carrying one RCS quad and the deployed HGA boom side.

parts.name: SM Aft Diagonal Brace +X to +Z
parts.role: Diagonal aft bay brace that triangulates the open Service Module frame.

parts.name: SM Aft Diagonal Brace -X to -Z
parts.role: Opposite aft bay brace that shows the cutaway frame remains structurally tied.

parts.name: SM Forward Diagonal Brace +X to -Z
parts.role: Forward diagonal brace tying the upper SM frame to the antenna-side quadrant.

parts.name: SM Forward Diagonal Brace -X to +Z
parts.role: Forward diagonal brace over the open bay, making the missing skin read as an intentional cutaway.

parts.role: Thin exterior skin stave that preserves the cylindrical outline without hiding the internal tanks.

parts.name: Narrow SM Skin Stave +X Lower
parts.role: Lower removable skin stave showing the SM bay cover line while leaving the SPS tanks visible.

parts.name: Narrow SM Skin Stave +Z Upper
parts.role: Upper +Z skin stave preserving the Apollo SM cylindrical bay pattern.

parts.name: Narrow SM Skin Stave +Z Lower

parts.name: Narrow SM Skin Stave -Z Lower
parts.role: Lower -Z skin stave that keeps the antenna-side silhouette without covering internal equipment.

parts.name: Open SIM Bay Floor
parts.role: Recessed J-mission science bay floor in the -X sector; the missing outer wall is intentional cutaway exposure.

parts.name: SIM Bay Upper Side Rail
parts.role: Upper exposed rail framing one edge of the open Scientific Instrument Module bay.

parts.name: SIM Bay Lower Side Rail
parts.role: Lower exposed rail framing the opposite edge of the SIM bay opening.

parts.name: SIM Mapping Camera Barrel
parts.role: Long-lens mapping camera barrel visible in the open SIM bay for lunar surface photography.

parts.name: SIM Mapping Camera Lens
parts.role: Dark circular lens at the end of the mapping camera, making the outward-looking instrument readable.

parts.name: SIM Panoramic Camera Barrel
parts.role: Panoramic camera barrel in the SIM bay; it points outward through the exposed -X cutaway.

parts.name: SIM Panoramic Camera Lens
parts.role: Dark lens cap on the panoramic camera showing the viewing direction from the SIM bay.

parts.name: SM Internal Equipment Shelf
parts.role: Thin internal shelf that locates tanks, fuel cells, and avionics within the Service Module frame.

parts.name: SM Avionics Electronics Box
parts.role: Visible electronics package on the shelf showing that guidance and power-control equipment sits inside the SM.

parts.name: Exposed Cryogenic Oxygen Tank
parts.role: Spherical cryogenic oxygen tank exposed by the cutaway so the SM life-support storage is legible.

parts.name: Exposed Cryogenic Hydrogen Tank
parts.role: Spherical cryogenic hydrogen tank feeding the fuel cells, shown inside the SM instead of hidden by a shell.

parts.name: Oxygen Tank Feed Line

parts.name: Hydrogen Tank Feed Line
parts.role: Small pipe routing hydrogen from the cryogenic tank toward the paired fuel cells.

parts.name: Fuel Cell Module A
parts.role: One rectangular fuel-cell package that generated Apollo electrical power and water from cryogenic reactants.

parts.name: Fuel Cell Module B

parts.name: SPS Fuel Tank B

parts.name: SPS Oxidizer Tank B

parts.name: SPS Oxidizer Feed Line B
